title: Coral and the Verdict
premise: Sebastian Ravensworth, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder will not happen — a murder the client insists is fated, foretold in documents Sebastian himself catalogued years ago. The trail leads to the cathedral's sealed crypt and the decade-old death of choir mistress Coral Vane, ruled accidental but whispered about ever since. As the statute of limitations on the original cover-up expires in six weeks, Sebastian discovers the 'future' murder is really the old one resurfacing: someone intends to kill the only living witness. To stop it, he must reopen the case everyone swore was closed, unmasking the killer among the cathedral's own canons — and choosing between protecting his mentor and delivering a truth the law can no longer touch.
about_author: Ulyana Nakamura is a former parish archivist who spent seven years cataloguing ecclesiastical records before turning to crime fiction full-time. She writes mysteries steeped in liturgical ritual, quiet English cities, and the moral weight of secrets kept for good reasons.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A pale stranger arrives at the archive office, pays triple rate, and asks Sebastian to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — naming the date, method, and victim. Sebastian accepts out of pride, not belief. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Locked Crypt, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He surveys St. Aldhelm's crypt, sealed since the Vane inquiry closed ten years ago, and finds the lock freshly scratched. The verger, Mrs. Okonkwo, warns him some doors stay shut for reasons. Beat: first hint the past is not resting.

chapters.title: Coral Vane, In Memoriam
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Reading the old files he himself archived, Sebastian reconstructs Coral Vane's death: found at the crypt stair base, ruled a fall. The file is complete — too complete, curated like a display case. Beat: the archivist notices what's missing.

chapters.title: A Date That Hasn't Come
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The client's predicted date falls three days after the statute expires on any Vane-era crime. Sebastian realizes the 'future murder' may be legally untouchable even if prevented. Beat: cold arithmetic replacing instinct.

chapters.title: The Choir Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He interviews surviving choristers; one, elderly Mr. Pell, hums a descant Coral composed and goes silent when asked about her last week alive. Beat: grief weaponized into silence.

chapters.title: Scratches on the Lock
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Comparing wax impressions, Sebastian confirms someone entered the crypt within the month — with a key pattern matching the deanery. Beat: suspicion moves inside the cloister.

chapters.title: Dean Ambrose's Hospitality
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The Dean offers tea and gentle deflection, revealing he signed the original closure order under pressure from above. He warns Sebastian off with genuine kindness. Beat: an ally who cannot afford to be one.

chapters.title: What the Client Didn't Say
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Tracing the retainer's payment, Sebastian finds it routed through a charity connected to Coral's estate. His client has a personal stake. Beat: betrayal of assumptions.

chapters.title: The Second Set of Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Hidden in a mislabeled box, Sebastian finds financial records showing the cathedral restoration fund bled dry the year Coral died. Beat: motive surfaces where everyone swore there was none.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo's Long Memory
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The verger finally speaks: she saw a light in the crypt the night Coral died and was paid to forget. She never spent the money. Beat: guilt as a forty-year debt.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Consulting a weary solicitor, Sebastian learns exactly which crimes expire when — and which don't. Murder has no clock; conspiracy might. Beat: hope and deadline entwined.

chapters.title: The Descant
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Decoding Coral's unfinished composition, Sebastian finds musical notation doubling as a coded ledger of the fund thefts. She knew. Beat: the victim becomes an investigator posthumously.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Him Home
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. After a near-miss on the close at night, Sebastian realizes his research is being watched. He begins keeping false working hours. Beat: hunter becomes hunted.

chapters.title: Canon Ferris Denies Everything
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The treasurer canon, smooth and wounded, produces immaculate alibis for the night Coral died — alibis corroborated only by each other. Beat: polished lies vs. paper truth.

chapters.title: The Client Surfaces
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian confronts his anonymous client: she is Coral's niece, raised on rumors, who received an anonymous letter predicting a second death — hers. Beat: fear made flesh; stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: A Threat in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The niece's letter matches stationery from the deanery office. Either the killer is taunting her or framing someone. Beat: paranoia reorganizes every relationship.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Breaking in legitimately via emergency access, Sebastian examines the stair where Coral fell and finds tool marks inconsistent with a simple fall — and a hidden niche behind the ossuary wall. Beat: physical evidence resurrected.

chapters.title: The Niche
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Inside: Coral's personal journal, half water-damaged, naming initials only — 'F.' and one more, smudged. Beat: triumph undercut by ambiguity.

chapters.title: Two Conspirators
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Cross-referencing initials against the ledgers, Sebastian narrows to Canon Ferris and one impossible candidate: his own mentor, Archdeacon Hale, who trained him. Beat: loyalty collides with evidence.

chapters.title: Hale's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian confronts Hale, who neither confesses nor denies, saying only: 'Some verdicts are mercy.' Beat: the floor drops out of Sebastian's world.

chapters.title: False Hours, True Trap
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Using his fake schedule as bait, Sebastian catches a follower — Mrs. Okonkwo's grandson, paid to scare him off by someone in the chapter. Beat: the net tightens upward.

chapters.title: The Restoration Fund's Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A retired banker confirms Hale countersigned the missing transfers — but claims Hale believed they were legitimate repairs. Someone forged context around him. Beat: mentor possibly duped, not guilty.

chapters.title: Ferris Moves First
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Canon Ferris accuses Sebastian publicly of desecrating the crypt, forcing the bishop to suspend his access. Beat: institutional power turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: Working From Outside
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Locked out, Sebastian works through the niece, the banker, and Pell's choir memories, assembling a timeline that places Ferris alone with Coral the final evening. Beat: exile sharpens method.

chapters.title: Pell Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Mr. Pell admits Coral showed him the coded descant and begged him to keep it safe; terrified, he hid it and let her face the thieves alone. Beat: witness guilt mirrors Sebastian's own.

chapters.title: The Predicted Date Approaches
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. With four days left, the niece receives a second letter moving the predicted murder up. Sebastian suspects the letters are pressure tactics — or a countdown. Beat: dread accelerates.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The verger gives Sebastian the envelope of hush money, untouched, and describes the figure she saw leaving the crypt: not tall enough to be Hale. Beat: one suspect eliminated, another confirmed by silhouette.

chapters.title: Ferris's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Ferris offers Sebastian a bribe dressed as a research grant, then, refused, hints the niece should leave town for her health. Beat: menace wearing velvet.

chapters.title: The Smudged Initial
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Under raking light, the journal's second initial resolves: not 'H' but 'D' — Dean Ambrose, whose signature closed the case. Beat: the kind ally becomes the deepest suspect.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Night
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Cornered gently, Ambrose admits he was there that night — called by Coral, arriving to find her fallen, and persuaded by Ferris to sign closure to protect the cathedral. Beat: complicity without malice; the machinery of cover-up exposed.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Fall
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Reenacting the stair geometry, Sebastian proves Coral was struck elsewhere and carried — and identifies the carrying route past the one door only Ferris could unlock. Beat: certainty achieved on paper.

chapters.title: The Niece Disappears
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The client vanishes from her hotel, leaving the second letter behind. Sebastian understands the 'future murder' was always about silencing her now. Beat: stakes become immediate and human.

chapters.title: Reading the Letters Again
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Forensic attention reveals both threat letters were typed on the same machine as Ferris's old sermons — he wrote the prophecy himself to control the timeline. Beat: the mystery's frame inverts.

chapters.title: Into the Crypt Again
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Acting on a decoy tip that the niece is held below, Sebastian descends at night, knowing it may be bait. Beat: deliberate walk into the dark.

chapters.title: Confrontation Among the Bones
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Ferris holds the niece at the stair base, intending a 'second fall' to mirror the first. Sebastian stalls him with the evidence aloud, buying seconds. Beat: terror managed by intellect.

chapters.title: The Verdict Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Okonkwo and Ambrose arrive; the verger's testimony and the descended lights trap Ferris as police, tipped by the solicitor, enter the crypt. Ferris breaks and confesses to striking Coral a decade ago. Beat: justice arrives by courage, not statute.

chapters.title: What Hale Knew
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Hale finally explains: he suspected for years and stayed silent to protect the institution — and Sebastian. Their rupture is honest but unrepaired. Beat: loyalty weighed against truth, truth winning at cost.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian writes the true account into the archive, sealing Coral's name with honor instead of erasure, and returns the untouched hush money to the poor box. Beat: the archivist restores the record.

chapters.title: Coral's Descant Sung
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At a memorial service, the choir performs Coral's completed descant, its coded ledger now plain history. The niece stays, employed in the archive. Beat: mourning transmuted into music.

chapters.title: The Next Client
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A new stranger climbs the archive stairs with an impossible request. Sebastian, changed, takes the case anyway — but this time asks the question he once skipped: who benefits from your story? Beat: resolution with the door left open.
